title: fix(ios-camera): restart audio capture session around AVAudioSession reconfigure
body:
## Description


Fixes muted audio in recordings on iOS when the user interacts with another audio app (Spotify, a phone call, Siri, an alarm) before or during a recording.

## Why

iOS sends an `AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification` when another app takes the shared audio session. Before this change the plugin had no observer for that notification, so:

1. The session stayed in an interrupted (deactivated) state — no mic input — but `captureOutput(_:didOutput:from:)` kept running and appended silent AAC buffers to the asset writer, producing a video with a flat-line audio track.
2. After the interruption ended, the audio capture session was never restarted, so subsequent recordings were also muted until the app was relaunched.

## Manual test plan

1. Start a recording.
2. Trigger an interruption (receive a phone call, start Spotify, or
   ask Siri a question) and then dismiss it.
3. Stop the recording — verify audio is present for the portion before
   the interruption.
4. Start a new recording immediately after the interruption — verify
   audio is present throughout.
5. Repeat with Bluetooth headset connected.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3881 Closes #4171

title: feat(inbox): redesign conversation screen and inbox previews

Closes #4287 ## Description End-to-end redesign of the DM screens (Messages tab and a single conversation). Touches the top "Contacts" carousel, the conversation list rows, the conversation header, the messages surface card, the message bubbles, the shared-video-in-DM card, the long-press action menus, and the report flow. Also fixes an inbox correctness bug (last-message preview was reading a denormalized column that could go stale), expands the app-bar icon button tap target to a true 48×48, unifies the DM-message and video report flows on one bottom sheet, and migrates eight DM-screen hardcoded English strings to \`context.l10n\`. ### A note on scope The supporting changes outside \`lib/screens/inbox\` might look unrelated to the DM-screen scope at first glance. While polishing the conversation header and the in-bubble shared-video card, I needed two cross-surface guarantees to also hold — those fixes only made sense applied consistently across every surface they touch, otherwise the same data would render differently on the conversation screen versus everywhere else. - \`lib/widgets/profile/profile_header_widget.dart\` — only a rename: \`_truncateNpubForDisplay\` (the helper that produces \`npub1xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx…\` for the profile screen subtitle) is now public so the conversation header can fall back to the same identifier shape when the participant has no NIP-05. Two surfaces, one helper. Letting the conversation header invent its own truncation would have meant the same user showed two different secondary identifiers depending on which screen you opened. - \`lib/widgets/report_content_dialog.dart\` — generalized to take either a video or an \`(eventId, authorPubkey)\` pair. The bottom sheet that opens from the home-feed video overlay's Report action and the bottom sheet that opens from a DM bubble's long-press > Report are now the same widget with the same UX (reason cards, "Other"-expands-to-details, in-sheet confirmation). The legacy \`ReportMessageDialog\` AlertDialog is gone. - \`packages/divine_ui/lib/src/app_bar/divine_app_bar_icon_button.dart\` — fixes a 40×40 tap target that should always have been 48×48 (the 4 px halo around the visible pill was previously decorative, not tappable). Caught while reviewing the conversation header; the fix applies everywhere \`DiVineAppBarIconButton\` is used. - \`packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart\` — the inbox preview was reading the conversations table's denormalized \`lastMessageContent\` / \`lastMessageTimestamp\`, which can go stale when an older gift wrap arrives after a newer one during backfill. Reworked the read pipeline to overlay the actual latest message from \`direct_messages\` on every emit; messages-table is the source of truth. In an ideal world these would be separate PRs. Given the redesign was already cross-cutting and the supporting changes are read-only or rename-level, they're shipped together — reviewers can take each section below as its own logical PR. The four supporting items have their own test coverage (\`dm_repository_test\` adds two overlay tests, the report-flow refactor reuses the existing \`report_content_dialog_test\` suite, the app-bar tap-target stays green against the existing \`divine_app_bar_icon_button_test\`). ## Screenshots ### Inbox — Contacts row (FollowingBar)

Inbox > Messages tab, scroll list — preview text shows the FIRST message of each conversation (the historic backfill stale value); avatar centered with column; shared-video DM previews show the raw URL alongside the title. ### Inbox — long-press actions sheet on a conversation row
Main This branch
Long-press any conversation row — actions sheet slides up but stops above the bottom nav bar, nav bar still visible. Same gesture — sheet covers the bottom nav bar entirely (routed through the root Navigator), matching the home-feed Comments / Report sheets.
### Conversation — header
Main This branch
Open any conversation — back button and three-dots button sit at the default 16 px insets, 80 px leading slot (22 px gap to the title); subtitle is empty when the participant has no NIP-05 handle. Same header — buttons sit 10 px from each edge, 74 px leading slot (16 px gap to the title), full 48×48 hit area on each pill (the 4 px halo around the visible 40×40 pill is now tappable); subtitle falls back to a truncated npub when there is no NIP-05 handle, matching the profile screen format.
### Conversation — messages surface card
Main This branch
Open a conversation — message area renders directly on the screen background; empty / loading state's content shrink-wraps to its column width and the surrounding shell looks like a narrow strip. Same screen — message list now sits inside a rounded surface-container-high card (32 px corners), spans the full screen width regardless of content. Tapping anywhere inside the card dismisses the keyboard.
### Conversation — message bubbles (text)
Main This branch
Open a conversation with mixed sent + received text messages — sent bubbles use surfaceContainer (low contrast against the surrounding card); received bubbles use neutral10; links inside both use VineTheme.info (blue-ish). 16 px gap below the newest bubble. Same conversation — sent bubbles use VineTheme.primaryAccessible (high-contrast dark green), received bubbles use VineTheme.surfaceContainer; links recolored: white in sent bubbles, primary green in received bubbles; the gap below the newest bubble stays 16 px.
### Conversation — shared-video DM card
Main This branch
Receive a shared video — the bubble shows the date, then a quoted title line, then a weirdly-cropped thumbnail, then the video title again, then optionally the URL. No author surface. Same shared video — date header always rendered; 248×350 thumbnail with 8 px corners; gradient overlay (transparent → 0.5 alpha VineTheme.backgroundColor, matching the home-feed bottom overlay) with the author display name (titleTinyFont) above the title (labelMediumFont) above the loop count (bodySmallFont); URL stripped; the sender's optional personal note renders below the thumbnail inside the same bubble pill; bubble caps at 280 px so the note wraps within the card footprint. the same divine.video share URL is detected the same way by the bubble preview and the long-press "Copy video URL" action (both use \`tryExtractDivineVideoUrl\` from \`lib/utils/divine_video_url.dart\`). - [ ] **Font scaling** — set system text size to maximum, scroll the Contacts row (names should wrap to 2 lines without clipping), open a conversation (header subtitle should stay within the 16 px gap to the back button; keyboard should dismiss. Bubble long-press and ListView scroll should still work. - [ ] **Shared-video DM resolution** — send a video to another user, then re-enter the conversation as the recipient; the thumbnail should resolve (it falls back to a tappable plain link only when \`VideoLinkPreviewCubit\` can't find the event on cache or relay). - [ ] **Report flow parity** — long-press a received message > Report; the bottom sheet's reasons, "Other" expand-to-details, and success confirmation should look and behave identically to the home-feed Report flow. The moderation DM the flow sends should carry \`DM Message Report\` + \`Message ID:\` labels (not \`Content Report\` + \`Event:\`). - [ ] **Inbox preview correctness** — open a conversation that previously showed the wrong (oldest) message in the inbox; back out; the preview should now show the latest message text. Re-sort by tapping a recent conversation that had a stale \`lastMessageTimestamp\` — it should move to the top. - [ ] **L10n switch** — change the device language to Spanish; the eight migrated keys should fall back to English (debt-set entries), but the surrounding strings (Mute, Report-on-conversation-row, Block, Remove) should render in Spanish — confirming \`context.l10n\` is wired correctly. - [ ] **CI green** — Format, Analyze, Tests, Generated Files, \`divine_ui\` coverage, plus the package-specific dm_repository suite (146 tests including the two new overlay-latest-messages tests).

title: refactor(notifications): delete legacy Riverpod stack (#3596)
body:
Closes #3596. Advances epic #4208.

## Summary

Final step of the dual-notification-system retirement. The legacy
Riverpod `relay_notifications_provider.dart` + `notification_model_converter.dart`
stack had exactly one remaining production consumer on `main` after
the four sibling PRs that landed today
(#4247 / #4271 / #4276 / #4277). This PR migrates that consumer
(`notification_settings_screen.dart`'s `_markAllAsRead`) to
`NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` and deletes the entire
legacy stack plus its five test files.

The BLoC-based `lib/notifications/` feature is now the only
notifications stack in the app.

## What changed

| Commit | Change |
|--------|--------|
| `docs(notifications)` | Brainstorm doc with the scope reasoning |
| `feat(l10n)` | New `notificationSettingsMarkAllAsReadFailed` ARB key + regen |
| `refactor(notifications)` | Settings screen → `NotificationRepository`; stale doc comment in `notification_realtime_bridge.dart` refreshed |
| `test(notifications)` | New `notification_settings_screen_test.dart` (success / failure / disabled) |
| `refactor(notifications)` | Delete 8 legacy files (provider + .g.dart + converter + 5 tests) |

**Net change: −4,595 LOC** (5,067 deletions, 472 insertions). 4× the issue's "~1,000 LOC" estimate.

## Behaviour delta

`RelayNotifications.markAllAsRead()` silently swallowed server errors and always showed a green "All notifications marked as read" snackbar. `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` rolls back its snapshot and rethrows on failure (PR #4034 → #4247 semantics). The settings screen now wraps the call in try/catch and surfaces failures as a red `VineTheme.error` snackbar with the new "Failed to mark all as read" copy. Strictly safer than the legacy "always confirm even when the write didn't reach the server" behaviour.

When `notificationRepositoryProvider` is null (early auth window), the action card's `onTap` is null — Material's built-in disabled affordance.

## Test plan

- [x] `dart format lib test integration_test` — clean
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — no issues
- [x] `dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` — no drift
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications/ test/screens/notification_settings_screen_test.dart test/screens/inbox/ test/blocs/notifications/ test/router/` — 471 passing (65 pre-existing skips)
- [ ] Manual iOS: Settings → Notifications → "Mark All as Read" → green snackbar; badge clears
- [ ] Manual iOS airplane mode: tap "Mark All as Read" → red `VineTheme.error` snackbar with "Failed to mark all as read"
- [ ] Manual Android: same two paths
- [ ] Manual account-switch: sign out → sign in fast → Settings → Notifications. Action card briefly disabled until repo wakes up; no crash

## Coverage

The 5 deleted test files (3,295 LOC) had their behaviour duplicated in `mobile/packages/notification_repository/test/` (refresh + mark-all-as-read + rollback + acceptRealtime, including the rollback semantics added by #4034) and in `test/notifications/` (BLoC feed, badge cubit, realtime bridge, view tests). No net coverage loss.

## Out of scope (filed as follow-ups after this PR ships)

1. `notification_settings_screen.dart` carries four unpersisted local flags (`_systemEnabled`, `_pushNotificationsEnabled`, `_soundEnabled`, `_vibrationEnabled`) whose Switch widgets do nothing across app restarts.
2. Audit whether per-type toggles (likes / comments / follows / mentions / reposts) actually gate notification ingestion or are decorative.

## Related

- Brainstorm: `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-12-issue3596-delete-dual-notification-system-brainstorm.md` (in this PR)
- Closes #3596
- Advances #4208 (parent: remove dual notification system and finish bloc cleanup)
- Built on: #4247 (unify unread state), #4271 (typed exceptions), #4276 (event-driven refresh), #4277 (dead screen + widget deletion)

- splits "Child Safety Violation" into three distinct user-facing report categories with distinct internal tags for independent routing

- **Child Sexual Abuse** — specifically for CSAM (NS-csam, NIP-56 `illegal`)

Zero user reports under the old "Child Safety Violation" label have been reportable CSAM. Conflating CSAM with general child concerns and age concerns prevents proper routing. This split enables each category to route to different workflows downstream.

title: fix(search): drop idle placeholder on Explore → Search with prefilled query
body:
## Summary

Tapping into Explore's search bar and typing 2+ characters auto-pushes `/search-results/:query` after a 300ms debounce. The destination then flashed **"Enter a search query / Discover something interesting"** for another ~300–600ms before BLoCs were dispatched and section skeletons appeared. On slow networks the window stretched, reading as a flash, error, or hang. This PR makes the destination drop the idle placeholder when a route arg query is pending, and dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously on AppBar mount so the BLoCs advance from `initial` this same frame.

Closes #3802. Companion to parent epic #3801.

## Root cause

`SearchResultsView` keyed the idle short-circuit on `VideoSearchBloc.state.status == initial` alone. That signal correctly identifies "no query entered" (the load-bearing PR #3199 fix for #3023's infinite skeleton) but does NOT distinguish it from "query just arrived as a route arg, AppBar dispatch is still pending its 300ms UI debounce."

## Changes

- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_view.dart` — add optional `String initialQuery = ''`. Gate the idle short-circuit on `initialQuery.trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so it matches the BLoC handlers' own gate exactly. Falls through to sections (whose own skeletons render on `initial || loading/searching` with empty results) when a searchable query is pending. Inline comment cites PR #3199 / #3023 so a future reader doesn't simplify the conditional back to the buggy form.
- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_page.dart` — pass `initialQuery` from `_SearchResultsBody` to `SearchResultsView` (1 line).
- `lib/screens/search_results/widgets/search_results_app_bar.dart` — reorder `initState` so the controller text is seeded BEFORE the listener is attached. When `initialQuery.isNotEmpty`, dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously to all four BLoCs. The BLoCs' `debounceRestartable` still applies; same-query dedup guards coalesce any late-arriving event. Focus model intentionally untouched — that's sibling issue #3020 / #3803 territory.

All 5 entry points to `SearchResultsPage` go through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: query)` (Explore auto-push, `@mention` link tap, universal link, deep link, GoRoute), so this fix applies uniformly.

### Commit history

1. `1f99c2b6` — initial fix.
2. `2407333d` — self-review follow-up: tighten the view's idle gate from `isEmpty` to `trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so reachable edge cases (whitespace-only or 1-char deep links like `/search-results/a` and `/search-results/%20%20`) don't render infinite skeletons (a #3023-class regression in the corner). Two extra regression tests pin the corrected behavior.

## Scope clarification

Per the issue body: "Do not collapse this issue into keyboard/focus behavior. They are related, but not identical." This PR is scoped to the intermediate-state symptom only. The focus and keyboard work belongs to:

- #3020 — keyboard collapses (assigned to @untreu2)
- #3803 — canonical focus behavior (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz)

The parent epic #3801 calls for these three children to land as one cohesive transition PR (Gate 2). I scoped this PR to #3802 alone; bundling is the epic driver's call.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/screens/search_results/` → **85 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/{video,user,hashtag,list}_search test/blocs/search_results_filter` → **119 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/explore_screen_pure_test.dart` → 12 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- [x] `dart format` → clean

New test coverage:
- `search_results_view_test.dart` — new `with non-empty initialQuery` group asserts `SearchSectionInitialState` does NOT render when `initialQuery` is non-empty + status is initial, and that the all-filter section list renders instead. Plus two regression tests pinning the whitespace-only and sub-min-length cases to the idle placeholder (cures the #3023-class edge case).
- `search_results_app_bar_test.dart` — adds missing `_MockListSearchBloc` mock (the existing setUp had a gap), plus three new tests: synchronous dispatch on non-empty `initialQuery`, NO dispatch on empty `initialQuery`, and no double-dispatch after the 300ms debounce window elapses.
- Existing idle-state tests preserved verbatim — PR #3199's load-bearing behavior is unchanged for the empty-query path.

## Manual device testing guide

### What changed (one-paragraph context for QA)

When you typed 2+ characters in Explore's search bar and the app auto-pushed to `/search-results/:query`, you saw a brief "Enter a search query / Discover something interesting" placeholder for ~300–600ms before search results loaded — especially noticeable on slow networks. After this fix, the destination shows section skeletons immediately and lands on real results once they arrive. The empty-query case (opening the search screen directly) still shows the "Enter a search query" placeholder as before.

### Build

Pick one:

- **Preview web build** (fastest, no local setup): open the `Mobile PR Preview` link from this PR's checks. The bot posts a `https://<hash>.openvine-app.pages.dev` URL on every push.
- **Local install** on the device:
  ```bash
  git fetch origin
  git checkout fix/3802-search-intermediate-state
  cd mobile
  flutter pub get
  flutter run --release   # release matters — debug mode is slower and masks the symptom
  ```
- **TestFlight / internal build** if one is cut later — pull the build tagged with this PR's SHA.

Notes:
- The bug is more visible in `release` than `debug` (debug is slow anyway, so any flash is harder to attribute).
- The bug is most visible on slow networks. Throttle to "Slow 3G" via iOS Settings → Developer → Network Link Conditioner (or Android Developer Options → Networking → Network type → "GPRS"), or use a proxy throttle.

### Golden path — primary repro from issue #3802

1. Launch the app. Sign in if needed.
2. Tap the **Explore** bottom-nav tab.
3. Tap the search bar at the top of Explore.
4. Type `hello` (or any 2+ character query). **Stop typing** and wait.
5. After ~300ms the app navigates to the search results screen.

What to look for (frame-by-frame):

| Frame | Before this fix (broken) | After this fix (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation completes | Screen renders with a centered search icon + **"Enter a search query"** + **"Discover something interesting"** | Screen renders with shimmer **skeletons** for People / Lists / Tags / Videos sections |
| ~300–600ms later | Skeletons appear (the placeholder fades) | (same skeletons continue, no flash transition) |
| Results arrive | Real results render | Real results render |

- **Pass criteria**: at no point during the transition does the "Enter a search query" copy appear.
- **Fail signal**: if you see "Enter a search query" or "Discover something interesting" even briefly, the fix didn't apply.

Tip: if you can't catch it visually, screen-record at 60 fps and step through frames.

### Slow-network case — the issue's "feels like a hang" complaint

Same steps as Golden path, but throttle to Slow 3G first.

- **Pass**: skeletons hold for as long as the network needs, then results land. No misleading "Enter a query" text. No fallback to an error state until/unless results genuinely fail.
- **Fail**: the "Enter a search query" copy appears, OR the screen looks empty/blank for any period.

### Direct entry to /search-results (regression check for #3023 — DO NOT skip)

This is the load-bearing case from PR #3199. **This must still work the OLD way.**

Two ways to trigger:

A. Universal/deep link with empty query — open the app from a `divine.video/search-results/` link (no query) if you can construct one, OR

B. In the running app: Explore → tap search bar → land on `/search-results/` with no query in the field.

- **Pass**: centered "Enter a search query" / "Discover something interesting" placeholder renders. **This is correct** — it was the #3023 fix.
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely (that's #3023 reopening).

### Edge cases — sub-min-length & whitespace-only query (the F1 finding addressed in commit 2)

Reachable via deep / universal links — try if you can construct them, otherwise skip:

1. Open `divine.video/search-results/a` (single character) — or build a URL pointing at `/search-results/a` and open it from another app.
2. Open `divine.video/search-results/%20%20%20` (whitespace-only, URL-encoded).

- **Pass for both**: idle placeholder "Enter a search query" renders. (BLoCs gate on `length >= 2` so sub-min queries never reach the network; the view correctly treats them as idle.)
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely.

### Other entry paths — same expected behavior

These all converge through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: ...)` so they should all behave consistently:

1. Tap an `@username` mention in a comment (links via `linkified_text`) — should land on search with the username pre-filled, **no misleading placeholder**.
2. Open the app from a universal link `https://divine.video/search-results/<query>` — same.
3. Open from a push-notification deep link with a search term — same.

- **Pass**: skeletons + results. No "Enter a search query" flash.

### Focus / keyboard — explicitly NOT in scope here

This fix does NOT change focus or keyboard behavior. Those are tracked separately in:
- **#3020** (keyboard collapses when typing in Explore → search page) — assigned to @untreu2
- **#3803** (canonical focus model) — assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz

title: fix(notifications): dedupe WS-first notifications against later REST loads
body:
## Description

Closes the symmetric gap left by PR #4247: a WebSocket arrival followed by a later REST pagination page containing the same Nostr event no longer duplicates the row (or duplicates a grouped contribution to an existing `(videoEventId, kind)` group).

### Root cause

`NotificationRepository._emitSnapshotForPage` deduped non-first pages by `existingIds = current.items.map((n) => n.id).toSet()`. WS-inserted items have `id = nostr_event_id` (bridge sets `model.id = event.id` → `RelayNotification.id = model.id` → `dedupeKey = id` since non-empty); REST-inserted items have `id = server_uuid` from `RelayNotification.fromJson(json)['id']`. The two ids never collide for the same logical event, so the same Nostr event flowed through both paths produced two snapshot rows.

PR #4247 closed the symmetric REST → WS direction by adding `_knownSourceEventIds` and the early return at `notification_repository.dart:260`. The reverse (WS → REST) had no equivalent gate inside `_emitSnapshotForPage`.

### Reproducing the bug (pre-PR)

1. Open inbox notifications on an account that can receive live notifications. The first REST page loads with cursor=`null` → `isFirstPage: true` → snapshot replaced (`notification_repository.dart:144`). `_lastCursor` is now non-null.
2. Stay on the inbox tab. From a second device, trigger a new notification (like, comment, follow) targeting the test account. The WS bridge (`notification_realtime_bridge.dart:64`) converts the realtime `NotificationModel` (with `id = event.id` = Nostr event id) into a `RelayNotification` (`id = sourceEventId = nostr_event_id`) and calls `acceptRealtime`. The row is prepended with `id = nostr_event_id`.
3. Scroll to the load-more threshold (`notifications_view.dart:75`) so `NotificationFeedLoadMore` fires. `getNotifications()` is called with the stored cursor → `isFirstPage: false` → APPEND path.
4. The REST page returns the same logical event with `id = server_uuid`, `sourceEventId = nostr_event_id`.
5. **Expected**: one row.
6. **Actual (pre-PR)**: two rows (or a duplicate contribution to an existing grouped video notification).

Refresh-from-scratch eventually clears the duplication because `refresh()` zeroes `_lastCursor` and the next emit is a full replace — so the bug is visible churn, not permanent corruption (the issue body says the same).

### Verifying the fix (post-PR)

Same steps 1–4. The pagination page no longer appends a duplicate:

- For standalone rows (`ActorNotification`): the new gate-2 `sourceEventIds` overlap detects that the REST item's `nostr_event_id` is already represented by the WS row and skips it.
- For grouped video notifications: gate-1 `(videoEventId, kind)` overlap merges the richer REST data into the existing WS row in place (preserving its position; rebuilding actors capped at `_maxGroupActors`; uniting `sourceEventIds`; `totalCount` = size of union).

### What changed

`mobile/packages/models/`:

- `NotificationItem` base gains `sourceEventIds: List<String>` (default `const []`). Subtypes pipe through ctor, `copyWith`, and `props`.

`mobile/packages/notification_repository/`:

- `_groupVideoAnchored`, `_mapActorAnchored`, and both `enrichOne` branches populate `sourceEventIds` from the underlying raws (skipping empties, mirroring the existing `_knownSourceEventIds` guard).
- `_mergeIntoExistingVideoGroup` unions `sourceEventIds` when a WS arrival merges into an existing group so the merged row carries every Nostr event it represents.
- New `_mergeAppendedVideoGroup` helper handles the symmetric "REST page → existing WS row" merge with locked semantics: set union for `sourceEventIds`; `totalCount` floored at `mergedActors.length` to keep the constructor invariant; existing-first actor order to match production pagination semantics; thumbnail / title / addressable id `_nonEmpty` fallback; **`commentText` picks from the side with the larger `timestamp`** (mirrors `_groupVideoAnchored`'s newest-wins and the surrounding `timestamp = max(...)` rule), falling back to the other side only when the newer side has no text.
- `_emitSnapshotForPage` for non-first pages now uses three gates: (1) `(videoEventId, type)` overlap → merge; (2) `sourceEventIds` overlap → skip; (3) `id` equality fallback → skip. First-page emit unchanged (REST first page is authoritative).

PR #4247's REST→WS guard (`_knownSourceEventIds` + `acceptRealtime` early return at line 260, plus the load-bearing test at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611`) is untouched.

### Follow-up

- **#4284** — techdebt: consolidate dedupe substrates (retire `_knownSourceEventIds` + `acceptRealtime` id-equality fallback into the new `sourceEventIds`-overlap source of truth). Tracked separately because the `refresh()`-then-WS semantic boundary needs its own regression test and the load-bearing test at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611` is the gate.

### Acceptance criteria mapping

- "WS-first → REST-later does not duplicate the same logical notification in the repository snapshot." — gates 1+2 in `_emitSnapshotForPage`.
- "Dedupe works for both standalone rows and grouped video notifications." — gates 1 (grouped) and 2 (standalone); covered by tests under `group('WS-first dedupe in page-merge (#4264)')`.
- "The chosen dedupe key is explicit and covered by tests." — typed `sourceEventIds: List<String>` on `NotificationItem`; new tests in both the model package and the repository package.
- "No regression to the existing REST-first → WS-later guard added in #4204." — `_knownSourceEventIds` and the `acceptRealtime` line-260 gate are untouched; PR #4247's test at `notification_repository_test.dart:1611` still passes verbatim.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4264

title: refactor(perf): replace polling timers with event-driven readiness signals (#3352)
body:
## Description

Three independent polling/timer coordination sites in `mobile/lib`
become event-driven. Closes the four acceptance criteria of #3352
without introducing new wall-clock timers or `Future.delayed`
workarounds.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3352

## Type of Change

- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

## What Changed

### Site A — `isNostrReady` (50 ms polling → one-shot `Completer`)

`isNostrReadyProvider` previously ran a `Timer.periodic(50ms, …)` until
`NostrClient.hasKeys` flipped true. Riverpod cannot observe that
transition through ref equality because `NostrClient.initialize()`
mutates the underlying `_nostr` instance in-place, so the workaround
was a busy poll on every cold start.

This PR exposes a one-shot `Future<void> get ready` on `NostrClient`
that resolves the first time `initialize()` completes.
`isNostrReadyProvider` now awaits that future once and invalidates
itself when it fires — zero idle wakeups on cold start. The
late-completion path is guarded against account-switch races by an
`identical(client, ...)` check before invalidating.

The sister polling site in `notificationServiceEnhanced` (a
`Future.delayed(500ms)` × 30 retry loop waiting for the same flip) is
replaced by the same `await client.ready` with a matching 15 s
timeout.

> Coordinated with PR #4162's broader `NostrSessionReadiness` redesign
> — that PR's compatibility shim for `isNostrReady` keeps the same
> provider name and value semantics, so this PR rebases cleanly on top
> of it.

### Site B — `RelayNotifications` (5-min `Timer` → FCM + lifecycle + pull)

After merged PR #4247 moved the badge + inbox feed onto
`NotificationRepository`'s reactive snapshot, the 5-min auto-refresh
`Timer` in `RelayNotifications` no longer drives any user-visible
state. The provider now refreshes on three explicit signals:

- **App resume** — `ref.listen<bool>(appForegroundProvider, …)` edge-
  triggers on the `false → true` transition. Re-emitting `true` (no
  edge) and `true → false` (pause) intentionally do nothing.
- **Foreground FCM message** — a subscription to
  `firebaseOnMessageProvider` calls `refresh()` whenever the divine
  push service delivers a foreground notification.
- **Explicit user action** — pull-to-refresh in
  `notifications_screen.dart` was already wired through `refresh()`.

Also removes the `_startAutoRefresh()` tail call inside `refresh()`
that quietly re-armed the timer, and the `ref.onResume` / `ref.onCancel`
timer hooks that surrounded it.

### Site C — `EmailVerificationCubit` (fixed 3 s → bounded backoff)

Replaces the fixed 3 s `Timer.periodic` with a recursive `Timer`
driven by a bounded backoff schedule (3, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 s, capped at
30 s). The 15-min total budget stays the same, but the total poll
count drops from ~300 to ~33 — a 10× reduction in idle wakeups for
users who never click the verification link. First poll still fires
at +3 s, preserving snappy UX for fast clicks.

The dispose-cancellation contract is now pinned by two new tests:
- cubit-level "close leaves no pending timers" (`fakeAsync` proves the
  recursive scheduler unwinds cleanly).
- screen-level "calls stopPolling when widget is removed from tree
  without nav" (proves the screen's own `dispose()` cancels — not
  just the GoRouter teardown).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `isNostrReadyProvider` invalidates from an explicit readiness
  signal, not a 50 ms timer.
- [x] Relay notifications refresh on realtime events, app resume, or
  explicit user action instead of a persistent timer where feasible.
- [x] Email verification polling has bounded backoff and tests for
  cancellation on dispose / navigation.
- [x] No new arbitrary `Future.delayed` or tight-timer coordination is
  introduced.

## Testing

- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- Scoped suites:
  - `test/blocs/email_verification` — 32 pass (4 new tests).
  - `test/screens/auth/email_verification_screen_test.dart` — 17 pass
    (1 new test).
  - `test/providers/relay_notifications_provider_test.dart`,
    `relay_notifications_insert_test.dart` — 46 pass.
  - `test/providers/relay_notifications_refresh_triggers_test.dart`
    — 5 pass (new file).
  - `test/providers/push_notification_sync_test.dart` — 6 pass.
  - `test/unit/providers/is_nostr_ready_provider_test.dart` — 7 pass
    (rewritten).
  - `test/providers/app_lifecycle_provider_test.dart` — 2 pass.
  - `test/notifications/**` — 250+ pass (regression sweep).
- Package: `mobile/packages/nostr_client` — 254 pass (5 new tests on
  the `ready` future, including error-path coverage).

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual on iOS: cold start with a previously-signed-in account
  and confirm no 50 ms-wakeup pattern appears in DevTools timeline.
- [ ] Manual on Android: background → foreground the app while on
  `/notifications-settings` and confirm the legacy notifications
  refresh once (not five-minute-later).
- [ ] Manual on iOS / Android: register a new account, leave the
  email unverified for >2 minutes, confirm OAuth poll count grows
  via the backoff schedule (not every 3 s).

## Coordination

- cc @dcadenas — Site A is logically subsumed by #4162's
  `NostrSessionReadiness` redesign. This PR's `NostrClient.ready`
  surface is additive and #4162 can land on top without conflict.
- cc @realmeylisdev (assignee) — #3352 is listed as related debt
  under #4208; this finishes the timer-cleanup half before the
  broader dual-system removal.

title: fix(notifications): throw typed exceptions from notification API methods
body:
## Description

`FunnelcakeApiClient.getNotifications` and `markNotificationsRead` silently caught all exceptions and non-200 responses, returning empty/failure DTOs instead of throwing the typed `FunnelcakeException` family that every other method in the file throws. Two layers of error-handling infrastructure were dead as a result:

- `NotificationRepository`'s mark-read rollback try/catch only fires on a throw, so the optimistic snapshot flip stayed in place even when the server returned 5xx — or when it returned `200` with `success: false`.
- `NotificationFeedBloc`'s `NotificationFeedStatus.failure` / `_FailureBody` retry widget / `notificationsFailedToLoad` l10n strings (translated to 16+ locales) only render when the repo throws, so users saw the empty state on a failed cold load — indistinguishable from a real empty inbox.

Both methods now follow the canonical `getVideosByAuthor` pattern: `isAvailable` guard, status-code throws of `FunnelcakeApiException`, `on TimeoutException` → `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`, `on FunnelcakeException { rethrow }`, generic `catch` → `FunnelcakeException`. `markNotificationsRead` additionally throws `FunnelcakeApiException(statusCode: 200, …)` when the server returns `200` with `success: false`, embedding the server-provided `error` string in the message so the repository rollback path fires consistently with the HTTP-error case. `NotificationRepository.getNotifications` swaps its swallow for a `rethrow` after preserving the structured `developer.log` line for triage. The BLoC and view layers need no changes — their failure paths were always correctly wired and just needed a real throw to react to.

**Existing tests** across `notification_repository_test.dart` and `notification_feed_bloc_test.dart` that stubbed the API to throw and asserted rollback / failure-status behavior **now exercise real production paths instead of dead code**.

Removes one bullet from #4208's "Relevant Debt" list.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3590

## Reproductions (pre-PR)

### Repro A — cold-load failure shows empty state instead of retry
1. Fresh launch in airplane mode; sign in.
2. Open Inbox → Notifications tab.
3. **Expected**: `_FailureBody` with "Failed to load notifications" + "Retry" button.
4. **Actual (pre-PR)**: empty state ("No notifications yet"), indistinguishable from a real empty inbox. The API silently returns `NotificationResponse(notifications: [], unreadCount: 0)`, the snapshot updates to empty, BLoC emits `loaded` status.

### Repro B — mark-read failure leaves optimistic flip in place
1. Open Inbox with one unread notification (badge=1).
2. Disable network.
3. Tap the notification.
4. **Expected**: row stays unread (rollback fires), badge stays at 1, error reaches `addError` for logging.
5. **Actual (pre-PR)**: row stays read (optimistic flip not rolled back), badge stays at 0. The API returns `MarkReadResponse(success: false, markedCount: 0)` instead of throwing, so the repository's rollback `catch` arm never executes.

### Repro C — refresh failure shows empty state
1. Load the inbox normally; some items appear.
2. Disable network; pull-to-refresh.
3. **Expected**: actionable retry UI.
4. **Actual (pre-PR)**: snapshot updates to empty (silent suppression), list shows "No notifications yet" replacing the previously visible items.

### Repro D — server-side soft-failure (200 / success:false) leaves optimistic flip in place
1. Open Inbox with one unread notification while the auth token has been server-rotated (so the relay rejects writes but returns a 200 with `{"success": false, "error": "token rejected"}`).
2. Tap the notification.
3. **Expected**: row stays unread, badge stays at 1, error reaches `addError`.
4. **Actual (pre-PR)**: row flips to read, badge zeroes, server actually rejected the write — the local read state diverges from server truth.

## Verification (post-PR)

- Repro A: `_FailureBody` renders with "Failed to load notifications" + "Retry" button. `NotificationFeedStatus.failure` finally fires.
- Repro B: row stays unread, badge stays at 1. The repository's rollback arm fires on the typed `FunnelcakeApiException` throw, restores the pre-write snapshot, then rethrows. The BLoC's `addError(e, s)` reaches `DivineBlocObserver` (not Crashlytics — per `error_handling.md` reportable matrix, network/IO/HTTP errors stay un-reported).
- Repro C: `_FailureBody` with retry replaces the misleading empty state. The user's data is preserved in the snapshot's `BehaviorSubject` value and reappears on a successful retry.
- Repro D: `markNotificationsRead` throws `FunnelcakeApiException(statusCode: 200, message: "Mark notifications read rejected by server: token rejected")`. The repository's rollback fires, snapshot returns to the pre-flip state, badge stays at 1.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/packages/funnelcake_api_client/lib/src/funnelcake_api_client.dart` | Rewrite `getNotifications` and `markNotificationsRead` to throw the typed `FunnelcakeException` family, mirroring `getVideosByAuthor`. `markNotificationsRead` additionally throws `FunnelcakeApiException(statusCode: 200, …)` on `200` with `success: false`. Add `isAvailable` guard parity. Update doc comments to canonical "Throws: …" blocks. |
| `mobile/packages/funnelcake_api_client/test/src/funnelcake_api_client_notification_test.dart` | Reshape obsolete silent-fail tests to throws-assertions; add new tests for `FunnelcakeNotConfiguredException`, `FunnelcakeTimeoutException`, and the `200 / success:false` soft-failure throw (with and without an `error` string). |
| `mobile/packages/notification_repository/lib/src/notification_repository.dart` | Replace `return NotificationPage.empty;` with `rethrow;` after the existing `developer.log`. Update dartdoc to document the rethrow contract. |
| `mobile/packages/notification_repository/test/src/notification_repository_test.dart` | Reshape `returns empty page on API error` → `rethrows on API error after logging` with assertion that `BehaviorSubject` preserves prior value across the throw. Add a `markAsRead` test pinning the soft-failure rollback contract end-to-end. |

No BLoC changes, no UI changes, no l10n changes — every consuming layer was already correct.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- **`_request<T>` helper extraction across all 24 methods**: #3586's scope.
- **Legacy provider/screen deletion**: #4208's scope.
- **`notification_repository` CI workflow**: this package was added in #4247 and has no dedicated workflow yet; flagged for a separate adjacent change.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

## Test plan

- [x] `dart format` — 0 changed
- [x] `flutter analyze packages/funnelcake_api_client packages/notification_repository` — no issues
- [x] `flutter test packages/funnelcake_api_client/test/src/funnelcake_api_client_notification_test.dart` — 22/22 pass (includes 2 new soft-failure throw tests)
- [x] `flutter test packages/notification_repository/test/src/notification_repository_test.dart` — 66/66 pass (includes new soft-failure rollback test)
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications test/blocs/notifications` — 116/116 pass
- [ ] Manual on iOS: Repros A, B, C with airplane mode toggling; Repro D against a server returning `200 / success:false`
- [ ] Manual on Android: same four reproductions
- [ ] Manual account-switch: sign out / sign in as different user with no notifications → confirm empty state still renders as "No notifications yet" (because the API returns 200 with an empty list and `success: true`, not a soft-failure)

title: feat(profile): upload a banner image from the profile setup screen
body:
Closes #4233

## Summary

- Adds a 3:1 banner image preview + camera/gallery upload UI on the
  profile setup screen, alongside a banner-scoped color picker.
- Uses the new bloc-driven upload pattern (mirrors the avatar's
  `pendingPictureUrl` / `persistedPictureUrl` shape).
- Image and color are mutually exclusive; selecting one clears the
  other at the bloc layer.
- Pre-fills from any existing `profile.banner` set in another Nostr
  client (URL or hex color).
- New ARB strings translated to all 17 locales (en + 16 non-English).

## Why

`profile_setup_screen` already lets users edit a banner *color* and
the rest of the app already *renders* banner images set in other
Nostr clients — but divine-mobile users couldn't *upload* an image
themselves and had to leave the app to update a banner.

## Architecture

- `ProfileEditorBloc` gains `InitialPersistedBannerSet`,
  `ProfileBannerUploadRequested`, `ProfileBannerColorSelected`,
  `ProfileBannerCleared` events; `PendingBannerStatus` +
  `BannerUploadError` enums; `pendingBannerUrl` / `pendingBannerHex`
  / `persistedBanner` / `bannerCleared` state fields; and an
  `effectiveBanner` getter.
- `_saveProfile` reads `state.effectiveBanner` (staged URL > staged
  hex > persisted, short-circuited to `null` when `bannerCleared`)
  so the UI no longer threads `banner:` through `ProfileSaved`.
- Save is gated on `pendingBannerStatus != uploading` (parallel to
  the avatar gate) so kind 0 isn't published with a stale banner.
- Banner color stored in bloc state as `String` hex
  (`pendingBannerHex`) rather than Flutter `Color` — the bloc layer
  is `dart:ui`-free; only the presentation layer converts at the
  render boundary via `colorFromBannerHex` / `hexFromColor` helpers.
- Banner-color parser extracted to `lib/utils/banner_color.dart`
  (`normalizeBannerHex`); `UserProfileUtils.profileBackgroundColor`
  delegates to it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Camera + gallery banner upload on iOS — sheet opens with both
  options; picks, uploads, snackbar success, banner persists after
  Save.
- [ ] Camera + gallery on Android — same.
- [ ] Toggle from color → image → color and confirm previews + Save
  payload.
- [ ] Clear a pre-existing Nostr-set banner image, Save → published
  kind 0 has `banner: null` (not the old value).
- [ ] Tap a swatch while a banner upload is in flight: swatch is
  visibly disabled and the tap is dropped; arriving upload
  completion does not silently overwrite anything.
- [ ] Pre-existing Nostr-set banner image renders in the preview
  and is preserved on Save when untouched.
- [ ] Pre-existing hex banner pre-selects the matching color swatch.
- [ ] CI green.

## Spec

`mobile/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-09-profile-banner-image-upload-design.md`

## Follow-up

Tracked separately, not in this PR:
- #4272 — client-side byte/dimension guard for image uploads
  (avatar + banner + bug-report image attach), to short-circuit
  oversized files before they enter the local processing pipeline.

title: fix(search): surface per-source fallback outcomes in people search (#3804)
body:
## Description

People search degraded silently. When NIP-50 relays timed out or the
Funnelcake REST API was unavailable, `UserSearchBloc` collapsed the
result into either `success` (with whatever accumulated) or `failure`,
and `PeopleSection` rendered "No results found for X" — visually
identical to a true miss. The lived consequence is #3791: users typed
a friend's username, saw an empty results screen, and concluded the
friend wasn't on Divine.

This PR threads per-source provenance from the repository all the way
to the UI:

- `ProfileRepository.searchUsersProgressive` now emits
  `Stream<ProgressiveSearchResult>` carrying both the profile list and
  a `Map<SearchSource, SearchSourceStatus>` recording each phase's
  outcome (success / failed / skipped, with latency and a typed
  failure reason).
- `UserSearchBloc` mirrors the map in state, promotes pending sources
  to `failed(timeout)` when the outer 20 s stream timeout fires, and
  exposes an `isDegradedEmpty` getter (`results.isEmpty AND any source
  failed`).
- `PeopleSection` routes degraded-empty to the existing
  `SearchSectionErrorState` (with Try-again button), instead of the
  misleading "No results found".
- Per-source latency / failure flows into a new
  `FeedPerformanceTracker.trackSearchSource` event so we can answer
  in the field whether NIP-50, Funnelcake, or the query itself is the
  culprit.
- New canonical contract doc at `mobile/docs/PEOPLE_SEARCH.md`
  (partial payment of #3627, the data-source-strategy doc gap from
  the parent epic).

The 5 s NIP-50 timeout is also lifted to a file-local constant for
symmetry with the other timeouts in `profile_repository.dart`, and
the bloc's outer 20 s timeout is lifted to
`search_constants.userSearchOuterTimeout`.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3791. Closes #3804. Refs #3801 (parent
epic), #3627 (data-source doc — partial), #3593 (suppressed catch

title: fix(notifications): unify unread state via reactive repository + badge cubit
body:
## Description

Promote `NotificationRepository` to a single source of truth for the inbox notifications feed, and add a thin `NotificationBadgeCubit` that mirrors the established `DmUnreadCountCubit` pattern. This eliminates the divergence class between the bottom-nav inbox badge, the inbox segmented-toggle count, and the per-row unread dot that PR #4165 only partially patched.

**The legacy Riverpod notifications stack is only partially retired in this PR.** No consumer reads `relayNotificationUnreadCountProvider` anymore, and the old `notification_realtime_bridge_provider.dart` has now been deleted. `relay_notifications_provider.dart` still remains because `notification_settings_screen.dart` still calls `relayNotificationsProvider.notifier.markAllAsRead()`, and `notifications_screen.dart` is still retained pending a follow-up route/test migration in **#4208** ("Last execution item under notifications").

**Related Issue:** Closes #4204

## Background

`NotificationFeedRealtimeReceived` and `NotificationFeedPushReceived` had **zero production producers** in `mobile/lib` (verified by grep). They were registered handlers + matching tests with no caller — the WS path entered only the legacy Riverpod cache via `notification_realtime_bridge_provider.dart:38`. PR #4165 closed the inbox-open badge case with a one-shot `_relaySynced` bridge but left three divergence vectors open. Investigation + brainstorm artifacts:

- `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-11-issue4204-unify-unread-state-brainstorm.md` (this PR)
- Prior brainstorm: `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-09-issue4144-notification-badge-desync-brainstorm.md`

## Reproducing the bug (pre-PR)

Three reproductions, each independently confirms a divergence vector this PR closes.

### Repro A — per-row tap leaves badge stale (matches #4048 Zendesk report)

1. Sign in as a user who has an unread notification (badge shows `1`).
2. Open the inbox → tap the Notifications tab. PR #4165's one-shot sync clears the badge to `0`; mark-all clears the row dots.
3. From a second device, trigger a new notification (like, follow, comment) targeting the test account. Badge increments back to `1`.
4. **While still on the inbox tab**, tap the new row.
5. **Expected**: badge decrements to `0`.
6. **Actual (pre-PR)**: badge stays at `1`. `_onItemTapped` flips the BLoC's row but never touches the Riverpod cache that powers the badge. Switching to Messages and back fires a fresh `_relaySynced` cycle and the badge finally clears — but the user has no signal that this is what was needed.

### Repro B — WS real-time arrival never reaches the list

1. Open the inbox. Everything synced.
2. From a second device, trigger a notification to the test account.
3. The WS bridge (`notification_realtime_bridge_provider.dart`) inserts the new row into the legacy Riverpod cache. Badge increments.
4. **Expected**: the new row appears at the top of the visible list.
5. **Actual (pre-PR)**: list does not update. `NotificationFeedRealtimeReceived` is registered on the BLoC but has zero production producers — the WS event never enters the bloc. Pull-to-refresh or backing out + re-entering the inbox is required to surface the row.

### Repro C — 5-min auto-refresh can race mark-all

1. Open the inbox; mark-all completes; badge=`0`.
2. Stay on the inbox for >5 minutes.
3. The legacy provider's auto-refresh timer fires `refresh()`.
4. If server write of mark-all hasn't fully propagated, the refresh returns `isRead: false` items and the badge can re-light.
5. **Expected**: badge stays at `0` once the user has viewed the inbox.
6. **Actual (pre-PR)**: intermittent badge re-lighting under transient server lag.

## Verifying the fix (post-PR)

- Repro A: badge decrements to `0` immediately when the row is tapped. `_onItemTapped` forwards to `repo.markAsRead([id])`, which optimistically flips the row in `_snapshot`, the snapshot stream emits, and both the feed bloc and the badge cubit pick up the new count.

- Repro C: the legacy provider's 5-min timer keeps running, but the user-visible unread count now comes from the repository snapshot rather than that timer-driven Riverpod cache.

## What changed

- **Repository**: `BehaviorSubject<NotificationPage>` snapshot + `watchSnapshot()` + `watchUnreadCount()` + `acceptRealtime(RelayNotification)`. Writes (`refresh`, `markAsRead`, `markAllAsRead`) route through the snapshot. PR #4034's rollback semantics moved to the repo layer (extended to `markAsRead` too).
- **New cubit**: `NotificationBadgeCubit` mirrors `DmUnreadCountCubit` in shape and lifecycle. Provided at two scopes — app shell (`main.dart`) for the bottom-nav badge, inbox-page (`inbox_page.dart`) for the segmented toggle — both keyed on `identityHashCode(repository)` for auth-flip safety.

- **BLoC**: subscribes to `repo.watchSnapshot()` in its constructor and projects via a private `_SnapshotChanged` event. Dead `NotificationFeedRealtimeReceived` / `NotificationFeedPushReceived` events + handlers deleted.
- **UI swap**: `vine_bottom_nav.dart:98` and `inbox_view.dart:66` swap from `ref.watch(relayNotificationUnreadCountProvider)` to `context.watch<NotificationBadgeCubit>().state`.
- **Page cleanup**: `_relaySynced` block deleted from `inbox_notifications_page.dart` and `notifications_page.dart`. `notifications_view.dart`'s `addPostFrameCallback` mark-all dispatch removed (page-level `_onStarted` handles it now).
- **Legacy cleanup**: deleted the dead `mobile/lib/providers/notification_realtime_bridge_provider.dart` shim and removed the unused `nostrClient` dependency from `NotificationRepository`.

## Out of scope (handled in #4208)

Per epic #4200's sequencing — #4204 is the first execution item, #4208 is the last — this PR does not delete the rest of the legacy stack. After this PR merges:

- `mobile/lib/providers/relay_notifications_provider.dart` still exists because `notification_settings_screen.dart` still uses it for the settings-screen "mark all read" action.

title: fix(collabs): make recipient accept/ignore observable in feed/metadata
body:
## Description

The kind-34238 collaborator acceptance protocol (settled in #4045) has had no read consumer on mobile since it shipped. Confirmed by grep: exactly one non-test mention of `34238` in the entire codebase (the constant). When the recipient taps Accept, the event publishes to the relay and falls into a void; when they tap Ignore, the local store is written and read only by the DM card that wrote it. Every feed surface (`CollaboratorAvatarRow`, `MetadataCollaboratorsSection`) renders `video.collaboratorPubkeys` straight from the kind-34236 tags, so the recipient appears already-attached before they act and stays that way regardless of which button they tap.

This PR wires the missing mobile read consumer so Accept and Ignore both have visible end-to-end effects, scoped narrowly per the v2 brainstorm (Approach F):

- **Inviter view (own-authored videos)**: `CollaboratorConfirmationRepository` opens a kind-34238 relay subscription scoped to `Filter(kinds: [34238], a: [videoAddress])`. When the recipient's acceptance event arrives, the avatar flips pending → confirmed on the inviter's feed/metadata surfaces within seconds. Pending entries render with reduced opacity + a "Pending" label on the metadata chip and a dimmed avatar in the overlay row.
- **Recipient view (any video they're tagged on)**: local invite store consultation flips their own avatar to confirmed (after Accept publish success) or hides it from their own view (after Ignore). No relay traffic for this path.
- **Third-party viewers**: unchanged. The broader "hide pending collaborators from non-inviter / non-collaborator viewers" goal defers to the Funnelcake `video_collaborators_current_data` read model that lives in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-25-collab-full-lifecycle.md`.

The new repository's data source can later swap from "relay subscription" to "Funnelcake confirmed-edges endpoint" without touching the cubit or any render site — composes with the lifecycle plan rather than duplicating it.

Repays the touched-path l10n debt in `metadata_user_chips.dart` (`Creator`, `Collaborators`, `Inspired by`, `Reposted by`) per #4192's engineering standard.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4192

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Architecture

- New `mobile/packages/collaborator_repository` package — `CollaboratorConfirmationRepository` owns the relay subscription, the cross-check against creator-side tags, and the local-store fast-path for the current user. Pure-Dart repository, Flutter-free.
- New `CollaboratorStatus` enum + `VideoCollaboratorStatus` value object in `models/`.
- New `VideoCollaboratorStatusCubit` keyed per `videoAddress`, exposes a `loading` → `ready`/`failure` state with a per-pubkey status map. No error strings in state.
- `collaboratorConfirmationRepositoryProvider` gated on `isNostrReadyProvider` (Pattern A from `state_management.md`) — returns `null` until ready so cubits never capture a stale Nostr client across auth flips.
- `BlocProvider<VideoCollaboratorStatusCubit>` keyed by `ValueKey((repo, videoAddress))` per the Riverpod-bridging rule in `state_management.md`.
- `CollaboratorInviteActionsCubit` gains an optional `confirmationRepository` and calls `markLocal(confirmed)` on accept-success and `markLocal(ignored)` on ignore.

## Out of scope (deferred to epic #4201 and the lifecycle plan)

- Funnelcake `video_collaborators_current_data` read model.
- Hide-pending-from-third-parties rendering (would change visible behavior for anyone viewing a video they're not the author or a collaborator on).
- Public decline signal — spec §"Accept Flow" pins ignore as local-only for v1.

## Tests

- `mobile/packages/models/test/src/collaborator_status_test.dart` (5 cases)
- `mobile/packages/collaborator_repository/test/src/collaborator_confirmation_repository_test.dart` (9 cases): kind-34238 echo flips pending → confirmed, rejects non-tagged-pubkey acceptances, ignores non-accepted statuses, recipient-view runs without relay traffic, `markLocal` emits immediately, `markLocal` rejects non-current-user writes, ref-counted subscribe/release, no relay sub when current user is not creator, `close` clears all state.
- `mobile/test/blocs/video_collaborator_status/video_collaborator_status_cubit_test.dart` (3 cases): success path, failure path with addError, release-on-close.
- `mobile/test/blocs/dm/conversation/collaborator_invite_actions_cubit_test.dart`: extended to verify `markLocal(confirmed)` runs on accept-success only and `markLocal(ignored)` runs on ignore.
- `mobile/test/widgets/video_feed_item/collaborator_avatar_row_test.dart` (1 case): hasCollaborators gate.
- `mobile/test/widgets/video_feed_item/metadata/metadata_expanded_sheet_test.dart` (2 cases): updated to the new `video:` parameter and to assert on l10n keys instead of hardcoded English.

## Manual test plan

1. Account A posts a video adding Account B as collaborator.
2. On A's device, open the video in the feed: avatar shows greyed + "Pending" decoration on the metadata sheet.
3. Switch to B. Open the DM with A. Verify the invite card shows Accept/Ignore.
4. Tap **Accept**: the card flips to "Accepted". Navigate to the video; verify B's avatar no longer shows the pending decoration (already confirmed via local store).
5. Switch back to A: within a few seconds the pending decoration on A's view of the video clears (kind-34238 echo). Re-open the metadata sheet to confirm.
6. Repeat with a new collaborator C, but tap **Ignore** on C's device. Verify the avatar disappears from C's view of the video. A's view continues to show the original behavior (third-party rendering is unchanged in this PR).

## l10n

New keys with English placeholder values for translators across all 18 locales:
- `videoCollaboratorPendingDecoration`, `videoCollaboratorPendingSemanticLabel`, `videoCollaboratorWithPendingSuffix`

title: fix(security): redact email PII from auth-flow logs (#4254)

## Description

Systematic redaction of email PII from auth-flow logs. Flagged in #3784's review ([point 4](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3784#issuecomment-4419836344)) but kept out of the emergency-security scope of that PR; this PR is the dedicated follow-up.

Audit of `origin/main` found **7 sites** that log email at info/warning level across `PendingVerificationService`, `DivineAuthCubit`, `EmailVerificationCubit`, and `EmailVerificationScreen`. Redacting only the one line Rabble flagged would create inconsistency without security benefit; this PR addresses all 7 sites via a single helper plus a broadened Crashlytics sanitizer.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4254

## What's in this PR

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `mobile/lib/utils/sensitive_uri_for_logs.dart` | New `redactEmailForLogs(String)` helper (Option B — partial-redact, preserves domain) |
| `mobile/lib/observability/reportable_error.dart` | Broaden `sanitizeForCrashReport` to strip emails alongside npub/nsec |
| `mobile/lib/services/pending_verification_service.dart` | Wrap 3 log call sites (save / expired / loaded) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/divine_auth/divine_auth_cubit.dart` | Wrap 2 log call sites (verification-required / password-reset) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/email_verification/email_verification_cubit.dart` | Wrap 1 log call site (startPolling) |
| `mobile/lib/screens/auth/email_verification_screen.dart` | Wrap 1 log call site (persisted auto-login path) |
| `mobile/test/unit/utils/sensitive_uri_for_logs_test.dart` | +9 cases for the new helper |
| `mobile/test/observability/reportable_error_test.dart` | +4 cases for email stripping in the Crashlytics path |
| `mobile/test/screens/auth/email_verification_screen_test.dart` | Regression test for persisted auto-login log redaction |

## Redaction strategy

Chose **Option B — partial** over **Option A — opaque** (`[REDACTED]`):

```text
user@example.com   → u***@example.com
alice@gmail.com    → a***@gmail.com
first.last+tag@x.y → f***@x.y
```

Rationale: preserves the domain so ops can spot patterns like "all gmail.com users are failing" without identifying individual accounts. Local-part collapses to a fixed-width `x***` mask regardless of length so original length isn't leaked.

Empty / malformed input (no `@`, empty local-part, domain without `.`) falls back to the existing `redactedSensitiveLogPlaceholder` (`[REDACTED]`).

title: perf(rebuilds): swap context.watch for context.select on three hot widgets

## Description

`context.watch<X>()` triggers a rebuild whenever any field of `X.state`
changes, even when the widget only reads one or two of them. This PR
replaces three such call sites with `context.select` projections so each
widget rebuilds only when the data it actually consumes changes.

### `profile_videos_grid.dart`

The highest-impact site — `BackgroundPublishState` emits on every upload
progress tick, and the previous `context.watch` made the entire profile
videos grid rebuild every tick (de-duplication loop, layout, etc.) even
though it only cares about the *shape* of the active upload list.

- Project state to `List<({String draftId, String? title, String? thumbnailPath})>`
  via `context.select`. Progress is intentionally excluded so progress
  ticks no longer rebuild the grid.
- ` _VideoGridUploadingTile` now subscribes to its own upload's progress
  via `context.select<BackgroundPublishBloc, double>(...)`, so only the
  affected tile rebuilds when its progress advances.

### `video_editor_draw_item_indicator.dart`

One-line swap — only reads `selectedTool` from a 7-field state. Now
rebuilds only when the selected tool changes (was also rebuilding on
undo/redo, color, and stroke-width changes).

### `profile_header_widget.dart`

Project `MyProfileBloc` state to `(profile, isInitialOrLoading)`. The
header now ignores `isFresh` / `extractedUsername` / `verifiedClaims` /
error-variant transitions that don't affect what it renders.

title: fix(invites): clear pending oauth session after consume failure
body:
Closes #4260

## Summary

- clear any persisted Divine OAuth session when invite activation fails after OAuth exchange
- route both invite-auth flows through the same cleanup path before showing invite recovery UI

OAuth exchange can complete before invite consume runs. This PR closes that gap instead of adding more retry behavior on top of undefined session semantics.

title: fix(security): strip BYOK nsec from Keycast OAuth wire (#3359)
body:
## Description

Phase 1 emergency block for #3359 — strips the user's nsec from the
Keycast OAuth registration wire on both channels:

- `body['nsec']` field in `POST /api/headless/register`
- `<random>.<nsec1...>` suffix embedded in the PKCE `code_verifier`
  (later POSTed as `code_verifier` to `/api/oauth/token`)

The fix removes the parameters from the `keycast_flutter` package API
entirely so a future caller cannot re-introduce the leak. A POSIX-grep
CI guard locks the rule in.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3359

**Cross-repo coordination:** divinevideo/keycast#197 tracks the
server-side proof-of-possession redesign that Phase 2 depends on.
This PR ships **without** preserving BYOK identity binding — that is
restored once Phase 2 lands.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ❌ Breaking change (the public `KeycastOAuth.headlessRegister` and `KeycastOAuth.getAuthorizationUrl` APIs no longer accept `nsec` — intentional, for security)

## Trade-off

Until Phase 2 ships, BYOK secure-account upgrades fall through to the
server's auto-generate path. The user's existing local pubkey identity
is **not preserved** across the upgrade, but the local nsec stays
on-device and never crosses the network. This is the intentional
emergency-block trade-off — stop the leak today, restore identity
preservation in Phase 2 (depends on divinevideo/keycast#197).

## Summary

- Paused-video overlay now renders the three playback toggles (compilations / mute / CC) above the play icon, applied uniformly across every surface that uses `PausedVideoPlayOverlay`.

title: chore: Gate Nostr side effects on session readiness
body:
## Description

Users could lose push registration on cold launch because auth could be ready before Nostr could sign yet.
This change separates identity readiness from Nostr readiness and makes signer-dependent work wait for the matching ready client.
That matters because push registration, notification preferences, and blocklist sync all publish Nostr events.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3929

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- [ ] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change

## Summary

Auth state now means the app knows who the user is.
It no longer means the Nostr client is ready to sign and publish.
The app now waits for an explicit ready session before running side effects that need the signer.

## What Changed

The flow now carries the ready pubkey and client together.
Work that publishes through Nostr rejects stale sessions and queues preferences until the matching session is ready.
Sign-out also runs outgoing push deregistration before signer teardown.

- Added `NostrSessionReadiness` and kept `isNostrReadyProvider` as a compatibility shim.
- Moved push registration, token refresh, preference publishing, push deregistration, and blocklist sync to ready-session or pre-teardown paths.
- Added warning-only wrappers so non-critical push publish failures do not escape async listeners.
- Added regression tests for cold launch, account switch, teardown ordering, queued preferences, and async error handling.

title: fix(dm): split optimistic into pendingOptimistic slice (#4193)
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #4193 — sent DMs were invisible in the live conversation until app restart on a freshly-searched user.
- Root cause: `_onMessageSent`'s in-memory optimistic and `_onStarted`'s watch-stream-driven projection both wrote to `state.messages`. A watch tick landing between the optimistic emit and the persistence transaction commit (the empty first tick on a fresh conversation, or any tick on a slow Keycast RPC signer) clobbered the bubble.
- Fix: move the in-flight optimistic into a new `state.pendingOptimistic` map keyed by `pendingId`. The watch path keeps replacing `state.messages` verbatim; `_onMessageSent` never touches that slice. A new `state.displayedMessages` getter merges the two for the UI.

## How the race fires (pre-fix)

1. User opens conversation → `BlocProvider` creates `ConversationBloc` with `..add(ConversationStarted())`.
2. `_onStarted` emits `(loading, [])`, then `await markConversationAsRead`, then `emit.forEach(watchMessages, …)` subscribes — `restartable()` bucket.
3. User taps send fast (typical when someone just searched a contact to message).
4. `_onMessageSent` runs in the `sequential()` bucket — concurrent with `_onStarted` — and emits `state.copyWith(messages: [optimistic, ...state.messages])`.
5. drift's `query.watch()` fires its initial tick: `[]` (no rows yet for a fresh conversation).
6. `emit.forEach.onData` replaces `state.messages` with `[]`. **Optimistic gone.**
7. `sendMessage` finishes → transaction commits → drift fires → `[persisted]` emitted. But on slow signers (Keycast RPC) or slow networks the gap between (5) and (7) is seconds. The user "observes" during that gap and sees an empty conversation.
8. Restart → fresh bloc → watch's first tick is `[persisted]` → user sees the message.

## Fix

```
state.messages           ← persisted truth, replaced verbatim by every watchMessages tick
state.pendingOptimistic  ← in-flight optimistic, keyed by pendingId, owned only by _onMessageSent
state.displayedMessages  ← getter; merges the two, preferring persisted on id collision
```

Strip rules:
- **sent / sentPartial**: remove the matching pending key. The watch tick brings the persisted row microseconds later (drift fires on transaction commit).
- **failed**: remove the matching pending key. `state.messages` stays untouched (no DB write happened).

Same `_onMessageSent` exception, retry, partial-delivery, and group-send shapes — only the slice that holds the optimistic moves. The brainstorm doc included in this PR maps the design 1:1 to #3909's planned `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)` projection, so this slice is easy to retire when that lands.

## Files

- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_state.dart` — new `pendingOptimistic` field, `displayedMessages` getter, `copyWith` parameter.
- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_bloc.dart` — `_onMessageSent` writes / strips `pendingOptimistic`; `_onStarted` unchanged.
- `mobile/lib/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view.dart` — `_ConversationContent` selector reads `state.displayedMessages`.
- `mobile/test/blocs/dm/conversation/conversation_bloc_test.dart` — state-shape + projection tests, **new race-pinning regression test driving a `StreamController<List<DmMessage>>`**, and migrated assertions on the existing send / fail / partial / group / retry / pendingId-uniqueness tests.
- `mobile/test/screens/inbox/conversation/conversation_view_test.dart` — new test: `MessageBubble` renders when only `pendingOptimistic` is populated.
- `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4193-dm-optimistic-watch-race-brainstorm.md` — design alternatives and rationale.

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `dart format` — clean.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/dm test/screens/inbox` — **324 / 324 passing**.

Tightened existing tests + added new ones:
- `conversation_bloc_test.dart`:
  - **NEW** `'optimistic survives a watchMessages tick that arrives mid-send (regression for #4193)'` — drives a real `StreamController<List<DmMessage>>`, pushes an empty tick during the awaited `sendMessage`, asserts `displayedMessages.length == 1` while `sendStatus == sending`. Pre-fix this would have observed `displayedMessages.isEmpty` at that frame.
  - **NEW** `'pendingOptimistic defaults to empty and participates in equality'` and `'displayedMessages projection'` group (4 tests covering empty fast-path, ordering, collision-with-persisted, unmodifiable view).
  - Migrated every send-side `s.messages.length` assertion to `s.displayedMessages.length` (user-visible) plus `s.pendingOptimistic` (in-flight tracking) so the two slices are pinned independently.
  - Rewrote the pendingId-uniqueness test to assert the strip semantics directly (`Map.remove(pendingId)`) using a seeded sibling pending — a cleaner contract than the prior list-walk-based scenario.
- `conversation_view_test.dart`:
  - **NEW** `'renders MessageBubble when only pendingOptimistic is populated (regression for #4193)'` — pumps a state with empty `messages` + non-empty `pendingOptimistic`, asserts `MessageBubble` is mounted and `EmptyConversation` is not.

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Search a fresh user via the inbox FAB on Android. Type a message. Tap send. Confirm the optimistic bubble appears immediately and stays visible.
- [ ] Verify the persisted row remains after pop + re-enter.
- [ ] Toggle airplane mode mid-send to force a failure → SnackBar shows, optimistic disappears, Retry works (existing #3908 path, no regression).

## What's deferred

- The principled fix from #3909 — `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)` at the repository layer with status-aware bubble UI — is the long-term destination. This PR is bug-scoped, and the slice it introduces maps 1:1 to the `pending` projection that #3909 will produce; switching is mechanical when the merged stream lands.

## Investigation + brainstorm

The full investigation (5-Whys, layer trace, alternative approaches, regression risk) was captured via `/investigate` and `/brainstorm` immediately before this PR. The brainstorm doc lives at `mobile/docs/brainstorm/2026-05-10-issue4193-dm-optimistic-watch-race-brainstorm.md`.

title: feat(dm): auto-sweep self-wrap-failed outgoing_dms via foreground retry service
body:
## Description

Closes #4124. Adds an `OutgoingDmRetryService` that sweeps the durable
`outgoing_dms` queue on every app-foreground transition and re-publishes
the missing self-wrap for any row in `recipient: sent / self: failed`
state via the `recoverSelfWrap` primitive landed in PR #4106.

Today that primitive is only invoked when the user manually taps the
partial-delivery SnackBar's Retry action. The SnackBar is ephemeral, so
dismissed taps and app-killed sessions leave self-wrap-failed rows
durably broken — silently breaking sender cross-device sync, the
*entire purpose* of NIP-17 self-wrapping.

The service mirrors `PendingActionService` one-for-one — same precedent
epic #3912 explicitly cites. It ships with a broad-shaped strategy
table but only the self-wrap-only entry wired today; rows in
`recipient: failed` state are enumerated and counted in logs to inform
the `recoverFullSend` follow-up (#4240).

**Related Issue:** Closes #4124. Follow-up: #4240. Parent epic: #3912.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

**`OutgoingDmRetryService` (`mobile/lib/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service.dart`)**
- New service. Subscribes to `appForegroundProvider`. On each foreground
  transition to `true`, runs one sweep over `getRetryableForOwner`.
- Per-row backoff via `OutgoingDmRetryConfig` — defaults match
  `PendingActionRetryConfig` verbatim (5 retries, 2s → 5min, 2× backoff).
  Backoff state is durable across app kill (the DAO already writes
  `last_attempt_at` on every `markXxxWrapStatus` / `incrementRetry`).
- Re-entrancy guard: a sweep already in progress short-circuits the
  next trigger.
- Strategy dispatch:
  - **State A** (`recipient: sent / self: failed`) → `recoverSelfWrap`.
    `incrementRetry` is called only on a real publish failure so
    transient repo-not-ready states don't burn the retry budget.
  - **State B** (`recipient: failed`) → log-and-count only. Pinned via
    `verifyNever(recoverSelfWrap(rumorId: 'b'))` in the contract test.
- Error handling: `StateError` (repo not initialized) aborts the pass
  without bumping retry; `ArgumentError` (row missing / foreign owner)
  is terminal-skip; other throws bump retry and continue.

**`outgoingDmRetryServiceProvider` (`mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart`)**
- New `@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)` factory. Returns null when
  `userPubkey` is null OR when `isNostrReadyProvider` is false (Pattern A
  from `state_management.md` — gates dependents on readiness instead of
  catching `StateError` inside the service).
- Bridges the synchronous `appForegroundProvider` notifier into a
  `Stream<bool>` via `ref.listen(..., fireImmediately: true)` plus a
  `StreamController`, so the service contract stays free of Riverpod
  types and is easy to drive from unit tests.

**`main.dart`**
- Single `ref.watch(outgoingDmRetryServiceProvider)` at app shell setup.
  The service has no UI consumer (it operates on the durable queue), so
  without an explicit read it would never be created.

**No DAO / repository / UI / BLoC / l10n / schema changes.** The DAO is
already retry-service-ready (`getRetryableForOwner({maxRetries})`,
`incrementRetry`, durable `last_attempt_at`, per-wrap error columns —
all from PR #3911).

## Test plan

Automated:
- [x] `dart format` — no changes.
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — clean.
- [x] `mobile/test/services/outgoing_dm_retry_service_test.dart` — 21
      new tests, all passing. Covers initialize/dispose, dispatch by row
      state, per-row backoff (skip / proceed / fresh), error handling
      (`StateError` aborts pass, `ArgumentError` skips row, generic
      throw bumps retry), re-entrancy guard, account scope, and
      `OutgoingDmRetryConfig.backoffFor` math.
- [x] `mobile/test/services/pending_action_service_test.dart` — 42
      tests, no regression in the precedent service.
- [x] `mobile/test/blocs/dm/` — 146 tests, no regression in DM blocs.
- [x] `mobile/packages/dm_repository` — 219 tests, no regression in
      `recoverSelfWrap`'s contract.
- [x] `mobile/test/providers/dm_repository_provider_test.dart` — 3
      tests, no regression in the DM provider's gift-wrap subscription
      lifecycle.

Pinning contracts added:
- The sweep never invokes `sendMessage` / `sendGroupMessage` / any
  recipient-publishing path (`verifyNever` on each in the
  "never republishes recipient wraps" group).
- `recipient: failed` rows are visible to `getRetryableForOwner` but
  are NOT dispatched to `recoverSelfWrap`.
- `incrementRetry` is called once per real publish failure and never
  on `StateError`/`ArgumentError` (the abort/skip paths).
- A second `sweep()` call while one is already in progress
  short-circuits without re-entering the loop.

Manual verification (please confirm during review):
- [ ] Force a self-wrap publish failure on a 1:1 send (e.g. block the
      second `publishEvent` round in a debug build), then **dismiss**
      the SnackBar without tapping Retry. Background and re-foreground
      the app — the row should be recovered automatically and the
      `outgoing_dms` row should be gone.
- [ ] App-kill the app between the recipient publish and the self-wrap
      publish (debug build). Re-launch. The cold-start foreground
      transition should fire one sweep; if the recipient publish had
      landed, the row should be recovered. (Caveat: a row in

      know whether the recipient publish landed — is out of scope for
      this PR's filter; it's covered by #4240's follow-up.)

      re-evaluated within its backoff window.

## Brainstorm + plan

The design rationale (why a foreground-only trigger; why the broad
service shape with only self-wrap-only recovery wired today; why
